en.title: Hunger Games Prequel Eyes 3D Conversion with Meta's VR Tech
en.summary: Lionsgate is partnering with Meta to bring 'The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping' to 3D screens, leveraging the tech giant's VR capabilities. This marks Meta's first studio collaboration for a 3D film conversion.
en.body:
The world of Panem is expanding, and this time, it's aiming for a more immersive future. Lionsgate has announced a fascinating partnership with Meta to bring **The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping** to life on 3D screens, with a particular focus on its integration with Meta's upcoming VR glasses. This collaboration is a significant step, marking Meta's first foray into working directly with a major studio on a 3D film conversion.

The prequel, set to premiere on November 20, 2026, will delve into the events of the 50th Hunger Games, also known as the Second Quarter Quell. This takes us 24 years before Katniss Everdeen's fateful journey, offering a glimpse into the brutal history of Panem and the early days of the Games. While specific casting details are still emerging, the film is slated to feature a star-studded ensemble including **Joseph Zada**, **Jesse Plemons**, **Elle Fanning**, **Kieran Culkin**, **Mckenna Grace**, **Whitney Peak**, **Maya Hawke**, **Kelvin Harrison Jr.**, **Ralph Fiennes**, and **Glenn Close**. The director's chair is reportedly being eyed by **Francis Lawrence**, who has a strong track record with the franchise, having helmed the latter half of the original series and the recent prequel, **The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes**.

## A New Dimension for Panem

The partnership with Meta is particularly intriguing. While the specifics of the 3D conversion process remain under wraps, the involvement of a company at the forefront of virtual reality suggests an ambition beyond traditional 3D theatrical releases. The mention of Meta's VR glasses hints at potential future integrations or exclusive viewing experiences, aiming to bridge the gap between cinema and immersive digital worlds. This move could signal a new strategy for how blockbuster films are released and consumed, especially by younger, tech-savvy audiences who are already accustomed to interactive entertainment. The film is expected to be a significant theatrical release, with a reported budget of $170-200 million, underscoring the studio's investment in this new chapter of the beloved franchise.

## Fans Ready for the Second Quarter Quell

For fans of **The Hunger Games** saga, **Sunrise on the Reaping** represents a chance to explore a pivotal, yet less-detailed, era of Panem's history. The Second Quarter Quell was a particularly brutal iteration of the Games, and revisiting it through a prequel offers fertile ground for storytelling. The prospect of a 3D release, coupled with Meta's VR technology, adds another layer of excitement. While some may be skeptical of new technological integrations, many fans are eager to see how these advancements can enhance the cinematic experience, making the world of Panem feel even more tangible and harrowing. The ensemble cast, featuring a mix of established stars and rising talents, also promises a compelling narrative performance, making this a highly anticipated event for the franchise's global fanbase.

## What's Next

**The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping** is scheduled for release on November 20, 2026, with a planned IMAX debut. Further details regarding the 3D conversion and any exclusive VR content are expected to be announced closer to the release date.
